basis: Mediastinal lymphoma is a lymphoid-cell malignancy; its location alone does not establish lung or heart involvement.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no other organ involvement established.
Primary cerebral lymphoma occupies brain tissue and is a lymphoid-cell malignancy.
Spinal cord and vertebral closure defect; persistent bladder and bowel denervation affect most patients, commonly >70%; hydrocephalus remains neurologic.
Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor arising in the cecum; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Volvulus affects the stomach; intrathoracic displacement does not itself establish pulmonary damage.
Inherited variation in phenformin metabolism; no intrinsic hepatic injury established. Drug-associated lactic acidosis does not justify another organ axis.
Malignant neoplasm involving the pleura, which belongs to the pulmonary axis; other sites depend on the individual tumor.

Congenital digit malformation with metacarpal and metatarsal fusion; cutaneous syndactyly is part of the limb defect.
Ependymal tumor arising within the central nervous system; rare extracranial tumors do not establish involvement.
Isolated inherited restrictive cardiomyopathy with myocardial dysfunction and cardiac chamber abnormalities.
White sponge nevus is defined by oral mucosal keratinization; the definition supports oral rather than cutaneous disease.
Malignant tumor arising from the peripheral nerve sheath; melanin does not establish skin involvement.
Localized inflammatory epidermal nevus; inflammation alone does not establish a systemic immune-mediated disease.
Cerebellar degeneration causes ataxia and abnormal eye movements; diplopia and nystagmus reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Syndrome defined by cleft lip and palate, lower lip pits, and limb deficiency defects.
Benign vascular tumor arising from blood vessels in the stomach.
Defined hypothalamic pathology drives excessive pituitary stimulation and thyroid hormone production.
Pituitary hormone excess defined by elevated prolactin; a circulating hormone abnormality is not a blood-cell disorder.
Inherited neural tube closure defects encompass anencephaly and spina bifida, affecting the CNS and vertebral development.
Malignant neoplasm of the paranasal sinuses, included in the airway axis; skull or orbital invasion is not universal.
Defining triad of skin nodules, osteochondrodystrophy and corneal dystrophy; gingival involvement lacks a qualifying frequency.
Renal cysts, fibrosis and insufficiency define disease; hypertension in 9/18 is a separately diagnosed complication.
Congenital neutrophil deficiency causes innate immunodeficiency; recurrent infections occur in 4/4, without a consistently affected additional organ.
